content.value_statement: Organizations struggle to map data practices to current standards and produce consistent governance documents. This skill structures assessments, implementation plans, and standards drafting.
actual_capabilities: Organizes applicable standards across data elements, datasets, business terms, and management practices.
Compares current practices with stated standard requirements and identifies priority gaps.
Builds phased implementation plans with activities, deliverables, evidence, and quality checks.
Drafts enterprise standard structures using the documented GB/T 1.1 framework.
Explains association standard participation from opportunity review through publication.
Creates compliance assessment outlines, standard systems, checklists, and training structures.
limitations: It does not verify whether cited standards remain current without authoritative external sources.
It does not issue legal, regulatory, certification, or accredited conformity opinions.
It cannot guarantee acceptance into an association, industry, or national standards project.
Cost and timeline estimates require validation for the organization, jurisdiction, and project.

use_cases.title: Build an applicable standards map
use_cases.description: Classify relevant standards, explain their purpose, and rank implementation priorities for a data governance program.

use_cases.title: Draft an enterprise data standard
use_cases.description: Create a review-ready structure for terminology, data quality, classification, registration, or management requirements.

use_cases.title: Assess association standard participation
use_cases.description: Evaluate participation routes, expected evidence, responsibilities, costs, timelines, and reputational risks.

prompt_templates.title: Identify relevant standards
prompt_templates.prompt: List standards relevant to [business scenario]. Group them by data elements, datasets, business terms, and management. Explain priority and applicability.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze standardization gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare our current practice [describe practice] with [named standard]. Create a gap list with evidence needed, priority, owner, and recommended action.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an enterprise standard
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an enterprise standard for [topic] using the documented GB/T 1.1 structure. Include scope, terms, requirements, methods, evidence, and appendices.

prompt_templates.title: Design a standards program
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a phased standards program for [organization]. Cover governance, applicable standards, implementation, conformity assessment, association participation, deliverables, dependencies, and risks.

output_examples.input: Map standards for a data asset registration initiative.
output: Priority 1: define data asset categories, identifiers, ownership fields, and registration evidence.
Priority 2: align quality measures with GB/T 36344 and classification controls with GB/T 43697.
Deliverables: applicable standards list, registration field standard, implementation plan, and review checklist.

output_examples.input: Outline an enterprise data quality standard.
output_examples.output: Proposed sections: scope, references, terms, quality dimensions, measurement rules, thresholds, exception handling, responsibilities, evidence, review cycle, and appendices.

output_examples.input: Assess whether we should join an association standard project.
output_examples.output: Evaluate strategic relevance, technical contribution, participation terms, total cost, staff capacity, publication rights, evidence of participation, and reputational risk before approval.

best_practices: Confirm each standard's status, scope, and effective date with an authoritative source.
Separate mandatory obligations, voluntary guidance, contractual commitments, and internal policy.
Attach owners, evidence, review criteria, and realistic milestones to every implementation action.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a standards list as proof of operational compliance.
Do not claim certification, legal approval, or official endorsement without valid evidence.
Do not join a drafting project only for attribution without meaningful technical contribution.

faq.question: What types of standards can this skill organize?
faq.answer: It covers national, industry, local, association, and enterprise standards related to data governance, quality, security, registration, and management.

faq.question: Can it draft a complete enterprise standard?
faq.answer: It can create a structured draft and review checklist. Qualified stakeholders must validate technical, legal, and organizational requirements.

faq.question: Does it confirm that a standard is current?
faq.answer: No. Verify status, amendments, replacements, and effective dates through authoritative standards sources before relying on any citation.

faq.question: Can it certify compliance?
faq.answer: No. It can organize a self-assessment, gaps, and evidence needs, but certification requires an authorized assessment body.

faq.question: How does it support association standard participation?
faq.answer: It structures opportunity review, application preparation, drafting contributions, meeting records, publication steps, expected costs, and risk checks.

faq.question: What information produces the best result?
faq.answer: Provide the business scenario, jurisdiction, current processes, target standards, available evidence, stakeholders, deadlines, and intended deliverables.
